models_evaluated: In-house deep learning AI platform for intracranial aneurysm detection on 3D TOF-MRA

links.outcome: Radiologist sensitivity and accuracy with versus without AI assistance across experience levels
links.effect: With AI, mean SE rose (residents 71.40% vs 88.37%; attendings 82.79% vs 93.26%; professors 90.07% vs 97.44%; P<0.05) and ACC rose; SP unchanged. Overreliance not assessed.
links.quote: Utilizing the AI assistance, six radiologists (i.e., two residents, two attendings and two professors) achieved statistically significant improvements in mean SE (residents: 71.40 % vs. 88.37 %; attendings: 82.79 % vs. 93.26 %; professors: 90.07 % vs. 97.44 %; P < 0.05) and ACC (residents: 85.29 % vs. 94.12 %; attendings: 91.76 % vs. 97.06 %; professors: 95.29 % vs. 98.82 %; P < 0.05) while no statistically significant change was observed in SP.

links.outcome: Effect of AI on radiologist diagnostic performance versus standalone AI and unaided reading
links.effect: Radiologists' mean SE increased 11.40%, SP 1.86%, ACC 5.88%, balanced ACC 6.63%, F1 7.89%, Net Benefit 12.52%, Brier score fell 0.06 with AI assistance.
links.quote: Overall, radiologists' mean SE increased by 11.40 %, mean SP increased by 1.86 %, and mean ACC increased by 5.88 %, mean balanced ACC promoted by 6.63 %, mean F1 score grew by 7.89 %, and Net Benefit rose by 12.52 %, with a concurrent decrease in mean Brier score declined by 0.06.

screen.reason: The study conducts a reader study comparing diagnostic performance of radiologists with and without AI assistance for detecting intracranial aneurysms on TOF-MRA.
